quests.instruction: Tap the sentence that is an opinion: something a person thinks or feels, not something you can check.
quests.prompt: A classmate is describing the school cafeteria. Which sentence is an opinion?
options: The cafeteria opens at 12:15 every day of the week.
The cafeteria pasta is the tastiest food in school.
There are twelve long tables in the main room.
Lunch costs three dollars for each student today.
quests.hint: Ask yourself: could someone measure or check this, or is it a personal judgement?
quests.explanation: 'Tastiest' is a judgement; different people will disagree. The other sentences give times, prices and numbers that anyone can check. Facts can be checked; opinions express what someone thinks.

quests.instruction: Select the TWO sentences that are facts (they can be checked).
quests.prompt: Mia is talking about her city library. Which two things she says are facts?
options: The library closes at 8 p.m. on weekdays.
The staff there are far too strict.
It has more than 20,000 books.
It is the nicest place in the city to study.
quests.hint: A fact could be proved true or false by looking at a sign, a list or a record.
quests.explanation: Closing time and number of books can be checked. 'Nicest' and 'too strict' are judgements that depend on the speaker's feelings.

quests.instruction: Tap the sentence that states a fact rather than an opinion.
quests.prompt: You are reading a travel blog about a train ride to the coast. Which sentence is a fact?
options: The seats are far more comfortable than bus seats.
Nobody should miss the views from the left window.
It is the most relaxing way to travel.
The train takes about two hours to reach the coast.
quests.hint: Look for the sentence that would be the same no matter who was travelling.
quests.explanation: The journey time is something a timetable can confirm. The other three sentences (comfortable, should, most relaxing) express the blogger's personal view.

quests.instruction: Choose the sentence in which the writer clearly shares a personal opinion.
quests.prompt: Look carefully: a sentence can start with 'I' and still only report a fact. Which sentence gives a personal opinion?
options: I read that most beaches here open in May.
In my opinion, summer is the best season for a holiday.
Many families travel in July and August.
Summer starts in June in many countries.
quests.hint: Check what comes after the opening words: a judgement, or information?
quests.explanation: 'The best season' is a judgement. 'I read that...' only reports information the writer found, so it is not the writer's opinion even though it starts with 'I'.

quests.instruction: Select the TWO phrases that could begin a sentence giving your own opinion.
quests.prompt: Complete the idea: '____ online classes are easier to fit into a busy week.'
options: The timetable says that
I think
Last year's survey showed that
In my view
quests.hint: Which openings tell the reader 'this is what I believe'?
quests.explanation: 'I think' and 'In my view' introduce a personal position. The other openings introduce information from someone else, so the sentence would sound like a report, not the writer's opinion.

quests.instruction: Choose the message that gives an opinion about the film.
quests.prompt: Ravi texts a friend after watching a film. Which message shares his opinion?
options: The lead actor was also in a comedy series.
Honestly, I felt the ending was too rushed.
It came out in cinemas last spring.
The film is two hours and ten minutes long.
quests.hint: Which message tells you how Ravi felt, not what the film is?
quests.explanation: 'Too rushed' is Ravi's judgement of the ending. Length, release date and cast are details anyone can look up.

quests.instruction: Choose the sentence that uses a word showing the writer's judgement.
quests.prompt: Four sentences describe a new bus stop. Which one includes a word of judgement?
options: The new bus stop is convenient for everyone.
The new bus stop has a metal roof.
The new bus stop was built in March.
The new bus stop is 200 metres from the school.
quests.hint: Find the word that says whether something is good or bad, not what it is.
quests.explanation: 'Convenient' says the stop is good for people, which is a judgement. Roof, distance and date simply describe or measure.

quests.instruction: Select the TWO words that express a judgement, not just a description.
quests.prompt: A customer is describing a café. Which two words show what she thinks of it?
options: overpriced
cosy
wooden
corner
quests.hint: Some words describe what you can see; others say how the writer rates it.
quests.explanation: 'Cosy' and 'overpriced' tell us how the customer rates the place. 'Wooden' and 'corner' describe features without saying whether they are good or bad.

quests.instruction: Choose the sentence that shows a NEGATIVE opinion about the delivery service.
quests.prompt: A customer is writing to a delivery company. Which sentence expresses a negative opinion?
options: The parcel arrived faster than we had expected.
The delivery was frustrating because of the long delay.
The driver texted us just before arriving.
The package was left at the front door again.
quests.hint: Which sentence tells you the customer was unhappy?
quests.explanation: 'Frustrating' clearly shows dissatisfaction. Leaving the parcel at the door is neutral, and the text message and the quick arrival are positive or neutral.

quests.instruction: Choose the sentence that gives an opinion about the topic.
quests.prompt: Topic: Homework for young students. Which sentence gives an opinion about this topic?
options: Homework is given on Mondays in Class 5.
Homework should be short for young students.
Some homework sheets have colourful pictures.
Many teachers check homework in the morning.
quests.hint: The sentence must judge what should or should not happen, not just describe it.
quests.explanation: 'Should be short' takes a position on homework. The remaining options describe how homework is currently given.

quests.instruction: Select the TWO sentences that give an opinion about the topic.
quests.prompt: Topic: Cycling to work. Which two sentences give an opinion about it?
options: A cycle lane runs along the river path.
Cycling to work is a great way to start the day.
The city should build wider bike lanes on the main road.
Helmets are sold at the shop near the station.
quests.hint: You need a judgement about cycling, not a detail about where things are.
quests.explanation: Both correct sentences judge cycling ('great', 'should build'). The other two are facts about locations and shops.

quests.instruction: Choose the opinion that is about the topic.
quests.prompt: Topic: Should the school have a swimming pool? All four sentences are opinions, but only one answers the topic. Which one?
options: The school garden looks lovely in spring.
The lunch menu needs more vegetarian choices.
Our science teacher is the funniest person I know.
A swimming pool would give students a healthy way to exercise.
quests.hint: Reread the topic question, then ask which sentence actually answers it.
quests.explanation: Only the pool sentence responds to the question. The others are opinions about the garden, a teacher and the menu, so they are off topic.

quests.instruction: Choose the sentence that takes a clear position on the question.
quests.prompt: Question: Should the town library open on Sundays? Which answer takes a clear side?
options: The library should open on Sundays.
There are different views about when libraries open.
Sundays could be an option for the library, maybe.
People have many ideas about Sunday opening.
quests.hint: A clear opinion says yes or no; it doesn't only mention that the question exists.
quests.explanation: The best sentence answers 'yes' directly. The alternatives avoid taking a side, so the reader still doesn't know what the writer thinks.

quests.instruction: Select the TWO sentences that each take a clear side.
quests.prompt: A class is discussing a four-day school week. Which two students state a clear position?
options: Some countries are trying different school timetables.
A four-day week would give students more time to rest.
I disagree with a four-day week because the lessons would be too long.
The idea of a shorter week comes up often.
quests.hint: Look for statements that say 'for' or 'against', not just 'this is being discussed'.
quests.explanation: The first two choose a side, one for and one against. The other two only mention the topic, so we can't tell what those students believe.

quests.instruction: Choose the sentence that expresses the writer's idea most clearly.
quests.prompt: A commuter posts: 'I sort of like the new bus route.' Which rewrite states the idea most clearly?
options: There is a new bus route in town now.
Many people have opinions about the new bus route.
The new bus route has some things going for it.
The new bus route is better than the old one for commuters.
quests.hint: Which version tells the reader exactly what the writer thinks?
quests.explanation: Saying it is 'better than the old one' gives a specific judgement. The other versions are vague, or they only report that a route or opinions exist.

quests.instruction: Choose the reason that best completes the opinion.
quests.prompt: 'I like living near a park because ____.'
options: Living near a park is something I like.
I can walk there and relax after work.
The park was built a long time ago.
My neighbours also live near the park.
quests.hint: A reason should answer the question 'Why do you like it?'.
quests.explanation: Walking there and relaxing explains the writer's feeling. The first option just repeats the opinion, and the other two are facts that don't explain why.

quests.instruction: Choose the reason that best supports the opinion.
quests.prompt: Opinion: Reading before bed is better than watching TV.
options: Reading is quiet and helps the mind slow down.
Many people own a television at home.
Books are sold in bookshops and online too.
Reading before bed is a habit I prefer.
quests.hint: Which sentence explains why reading is better, not just that it exists?
quests.explanation: The calming effect explains the 'better'. The other options mention TVs and bookshops without explaining, or restate the writer's preference.

quests.instruction: Select the TWO reasons that support the opinion.
quests.prompt: Opinion: Our office should have a quiet room.
options: People can focus better on difficult tasks.
The office already has three meeting rooms.
Private phone calls are easier to make.
Rooms can be painted in many different colours.
quests.hint: Which sentences say what a quiet room would do for the people who work there?
quests.explanation: Concentration and private calls are benefits of a quiet room. The number of existing rooms and paint colours don't explain why a quiet room is needed.

quests.instruction: Find the part of the sentence that gives the reason.
quests.prompt: 'Our town should build more bike lanes because many cyclists feel unsafe on busy roads.' Which part is the reason?
options: should build more bike lanes
many cyclists feel unsafe on busy roads
more bike lanes
our town should build more bike lanes
quests.hint: The reason is the part that answers 'Why should the town do this?'.
quests.explanation: What comes after 'because' explains why. The part before it is the opinion itself.

quests.instruction: Choose the statement that is a reason for the opinion, not another opinion.
quests.prompt: Opinion: Schools should teach students how to cook.
options: Cooking classes would be a great idea.
Some schools already have a kitchen room.
Schools should also teach gardening.
Students will need to feed themselves as adults.
quests.hint: A reason gives a why. Another opinion only says more of what someone believes.
quests.explanation: Needing to feed themselves gives a real explanation. The other options restate the opinion, add a new opinion, or mention a fact that doesn't say why.

quests.instruction: Select the THREE statements that give reasons. One is only another opinion.
quests.prompt: A student argues that phones should stay in lockers during lessons.
options: Notifications interrupt students' attention.
Class would be much better without phones.
Students can be tempted to text during lessons.
A phone can be used to cheat during a test.
quests.hint: Which statements explain why phones cause problems in lessons?
quests.explanation: Interruptions, texting and cheating each explain a problem. 'Class would be much better without phones' repeats the opinion in different words without adding a reason.

quests.instruction: Select the TWO statements that SUPPORT the opinion.
quests.prompt: Opinion: Cities should have more public drinking fountains.
options: Fountains let people refill bottles, not buy new ones.
Fountains cost a lot of money to install and clean.
Free water makes hot days easier for walkers.
Some fountains are rarely used and break down easily.
quests.hint: Support means the statement helps the opinion. Sort out which ones argue for it.
quests.explanation: Refilling bottles and helping people in the heat argue for fountains. Cost and breakage are reasons against the idea.

quests.instruction: Tap the statement that argues AGAINST the opinion.
quests.prompt: Opinion: Shops should stay open late on Sundays.
options: Late opening would bring more customers into town.
Families could shop together after a day out.
Staff would lose their only relaxed evening of the week.
Shoppers with weekday jobs could visit at a calmer time.
quests.hint: Three statements give benefits. One describes a cost.
quests.explanation: Losing a free evening is a downside for staff, so it opposes late opening. The others describe benefits that support it.

quests.instruction: Select the TWO statements that OPPOSE the opinion.
quests.prompt: Opinion: Every student should learn a musical instrument.
options: Music practice helps students learn to focus better.
Lessons and instruments cost too much for some families.
Practice might take time away from other subjects.
Playing in a group builds teamwork and confidence.
quests.hint: Find the two that give reasons why the idea might not work.
quests.explanation: Cost and time are drawbacks that argue against making it universal. Focus and teamwork are benefits that support the opinion.

quests.instruction: Choose the statement that does NOT relate to the opinion.
quests.prompt: Opinion: Our school should plant a vegetable garden. Three statements are reasons for it. Which one is off topic?
options: Students could learn where food comes from.
Being outdoors is a nice break from lessons.
Fresh vegetables could be used in the canteen.
The school building was painted last summer.
quests.hint: Test each statement: does it help explain why a garden is a good idea?
quests.explanation: The paint job has nothing to do with a garden. The other three each give a benefit of growing vegetables at school.

quests.instruction: Choose the statement that is a relevant reason for the opinion.
quests.prompt: Opinion: Buses should run more often at weekends.
options: Many people without cars depend on buses to get to work and visit family.
Buses were first used in cities over a hundred years ago, long before most of today's routes were planned.
Our usual bus driver has a friendly smile and always says good morning to the passengers who board.
The bus station has a large clock above the entrance, which most passengers can see from the street.
quests.hint: Three statements are true, but only one explains why weekend buses matter.
quests.explanation: People who rely on buses need frequent weekend service. The other statements are true but have no link to how often buses run.

quests.instruction: Select the TWO reasons that really support the opinion.
quests.prompt: Opinion: A company should offer free parking to its staff.
options: The company has offices in three different cities.
Parking fees can take a large part of a low salary.
Many staff members enjoy walking at lunchtime.
Some employees have no other practical way to arrive on time.
quests.hint: Ask whether each statement connects to the cost or need of parking.
quests.explanation: Need and cost are directly linked to parking. Office locations and lunchtime walks are true but don't explain why parking should be free.

quests.instruction: Choose the sentence that gives both an opinion and a reason.
quests.prompt: Which of these sentences contains an opinion AND a reason for it?
options: Trains beat planes on short trips because there is no security queue.
Planes fly faster than trains over very long distances.
Trains leave from the central station every hour of the day.
Trains are better than planes for short trips overall.
quests.hint: Look for a sentence that says what the writer thinks and why.
quests.explanation: The first sentence says trains are better and explains why. The second gives only the opinion, and the last two are facts.

quests.instruction: Select the TWO sentences that would fit in a short paragraph supporting the opinion.
quests.prompt: Opinion: A neighbourhood should have a weekly farmers' market.
options: The old town hall was rebuilt in the year 1990.
It gives neighbours a regular place to meet.
Supermarkets in the area open early in the morning.
Residents can buy fresh food from local growers.
quests.hint: Choose sentences that would make a reader agree with the market idea.
quests.explanation: Fresh food and community contact are benefits of a market. The town hall and supermarket hours don't help the argument.

quests.instruction: Put the sentences in the best order to make a short opinion text.
quests.prompt: Arrange these four sentences into a clear opinion paragraph.
options: That is why I think offices should welcome greenery.
I believe every office should have a plant or two.
For example, my team's area feels friendlier since we added a small fern.
Plants make a room feel fresher and more welcoming.
quests.hint: Start with what the writer thinks. End with a sentence that returns to it.
quests.explanation: A clear text states the opinion first, gives a reason, shows a real example, then finishes by restating the opinion.
